text:
Ada: FYI seeing a bunch of OOMs on prod-gpu-pool around 10:12 UTC, all during high-batch long-context traffic. started ~10:11 and affected ~7 pods. anyone on call?

Miguel: saw the alerts. allocator reserve failing (ENOMEN) when kernel-selector switches to the long-seq path. looks like buffer reuse + fragmentation combo.

Sophia: attaching quick profiling pointer: gputop snapshot shows steady kernel WS growth before OOM. likely workspace sizing for the new kernel variant is underestimating temporary allocs. https://internal/profiles/3187654322

Chris: logs snippet: `Allocator::try_reserve(1.1G) -> ENOMEM` then `KernelSelector::switch_to(long_seq)` and then spikes. suspect we retained freed slabs due to reuse refcounts.

Ada: repro steps local: run loadtest --seq_len=4096 --batch=8 --kv_coldstart=1 on canary, you'll hit in ~3-5 min.

Miguel: immediate mitigations to push now:
1) toggle feature flag to disable kernel autoswitch on affected nodes: `runtime.kernel_autoswitch=false`
2) apply route-level small-batch cap: `batch.max_size=4` for high-ctx routes
3) enable aggressive KV eviction TTL: `kv.eviction_policy=aggressive, kv.hot_threshold=0.6`

Sophia: commands (apply to kube namespace `runtime-prod`):
```bash
kubectl -n runtime-prod patch cm runtime-flags --patch '{"data":{"kernel_autoswitch":"false"}}'
kubectl -n runtime-prod rollout restart ds/gpu-runtime-nvidia
```

Chris: also add a soft circuit breaker so allocator failures return 503 + Retry-After and trigger fallback to quantized-4bit variant. simple pseudocode:
```
if (!allocator.try_reserve(sz)) {
  metrics.counter("allocator.reserve.fail")++
  return fallback(quantized_variant) OR 503(RETRY_AFTER=5)
}
```

Ada: pushed the config patch to 5 nodes (canary subset) — memory climb stopped on those. alerts muted for that subset.

runtime-bot: rollout/daemonset/gpu-runtime-nvidia patched (canary subset) — status: SUCCESS ✅

Miguel: follow-up engineering actions:
- quick: add guard in kernel-selector to estimate temp scratch more conservatively for long-seq path
- medium: allocator compaction + slab merge on free to reduce fragmentation
- long: revisit buffer-reuse refcounting and add an opt-in compacting allocator mode
I can start an RFC today for slab-merge and a perf test harness.

Sophia: I'll add the repro and the gputop snapshot to the incident page and mark this as "redline-buffer-shepherd" mitigation steps.

Ada: thanks team. adding to runbook: if OOM pattern matches kernel-switch + reserve ENOMEM -> roll kernel_autoswitch flag to false, throttle batch sizes, enable aggressive kv eviction, and enable fallback to smaller/quantized model. close when stable for 4h. :thumbsup:
